questions.q: Why does this lesson say the board's funding approval from Lesson 20 is 'a budget line, not a rollout plan'?
options: Because the board actually denied the funding
Because scoping the next phase requires naming specifically which segment is next, what gets built in what order, and which dependencies exist — none of which a funding approval by itself specifies
Because Hartwell has no budget process at all
Because the pilot segment was never actually completed
questions.explain: Without naming the segment, build order, and dependencies, 'expand the pilot' is a slogan with a budget attached, not an actual plan.

questions.q: Which horizon does extending Conditional Access and MFA to the second segment's engineering workstations belong to, and why?
options: Long-haul, because it requires a multi-year identity rebuild first
Quick win, because it reduces real risk immediately without waiting on a full identity rebuild
Foundational, because it is the dependency everything else needs
It doesn't fit any horizon in this model
questions.explain: Quick wins are near-term changes that reduce risk on their own, which is exactly what extending MFA/Conditional Access does here.

questions.q: What new dependency does this phase carry that the original OT/SCADA pilot didn't have to think about?
options: The need to disable all break-glass access company-wide
The corrected, dual-check audit methodology from Lesson 19 must apply to the new segment from the start, not get bolted on after a second audit finds the same kind of gap again
The requirement to migrate away from AWS entirely
A requirement to skip identity work and segment first
questions.explain: Rolling out the new segment with the old group-membership-only audit approach would mean repeating the exact mistake Lesson 19's AAR just documented, this time on equipment with real physical stakes.

questions.q: What does this lesson say makes a roadmap line defensible, rather than just optimistic?
options: Naming the vendor who will implement it
Naming specifically what changes for users and attackers once it ships — for example, that standing local-admin access no longer exists outside a time-boxed, audited break-glass workflow
Keeping the roadmap line as vague as possible so it can't be proven wrong
Listing only the total dollar cost of the initiative
questions.explain: Specificity about what concretely changes is what makes a roadmap line checkable later, rather than just a hopeful label now.

questions.q: What scheduling fact does scoping this phase surface, which sets up Lesson 23's conflict?
options: Hartwell has unlimited maintenance windows available at any time
The foundational identity and segmentation work on physical OT equipment can only be safely deployed during a planned maintenance outage, and only one is scheduled in the near term
The board has requested the rollout be cancelled entirely
Mara Voss is unavailable for the next six months
questions.explain: That single scheduling constraint — one maintenance window, foundational work that needs it — is the real source of the speed-versus-control tension in the next lesson.
